questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis for 2 weeks. The base is clean, indurated, and non-tender. Inguinal lymph nodes are rubbery and non-tender. Which test will give the earliest positive result?
questions.exp: Dark field microscopy of serous exudate from the ulcer base directly visualizes Treponema pallidum spirochetes and is positive at the time of ulcer appearance, before serological tests turn positive.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with depigmented macules on the face with loss of sensation. Slit skin smear shows no organisms. Skin biopsy shows granuloma formation around dermal nerves with nerve destruction. What is the leprosy classification?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) shows well-formed epithelioid granulomas around and within nerves (nerve destruction), negative slit skin smear (paucibacillary), few hypopigmented anaesthetic patches.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic patient develops a rapidly spreading necrotizing infection of the scrotum and perineum with crepitus on palpation. Which organism is MOST commonly implicated?
questions.exp: Fournier's gangrene is a polymicrobial necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum caused by synergistic action of mixed aerobic (E. coli, Klebsiella, Pseudomonas) and anaerobic (Bacteroides, Peptostreptococcus) organisms.

questions.q: A 22-year-old man presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the dorsum of his right hand following a thorn prick. Tzanck smear is negative. Culture grows a mold with broad non-septate hyphae at 25°C but yeast forms at 37°C. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Sporothrix schenckii is a thermally dimorphic fungus (mold at 25°C, yeast at 37°C) causing sporotrichosis, classically after thorn/plant injury, with lymphocutaneous spread.

questions.q: A patient with pemphigus vulgaris is started on systemic steroids. Which of the following best reflects the target of the autoantibody in this condition?
opts: Laminin 332 in the basement membrane zone
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris is caused by IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 3 (primarily), leading to acantholysis in the suprabasal layer with intraepidermal blistering.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with tense bullae on an erythematous base involving the trunk and extremities with intense pruritus. Immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposits at the basement membrane zone. Which antigen is targeted?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid is characterized by autoantibodies against BP180 (and BP230) at the hemidesmosome level, causing subepidermal blistering. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ.

questions.q: A 30-year-old presents with scaly plaques on scalp and elbows. Histopathology shows parakeratosis, elongated rete ridges, thinned suprapapillary plate, and neutrophilic microabscesses in the stratum corneum. What are these microabscesses called?
questions.exp: Munro microabscesses are collections of neutrophils within the parakeratotic stratum corneum, pathognomonic of psoriasis. Pautrier microabscesses are seen in mycosis fungoides.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman with SLE presents with a butterfly rash, photosensitivity, and a positive anti-dsDNA. She develops discoid lesions with follicular plugging and atrophic scarring. Which antibody is most specific for SLE?
questions.exp: Anti-Smith (anti-Sm) antibody is the MOST specific antibody for SLE, though anti-dsDNA is more sensitive and correlates with disease activity/nephritis.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with a plaque of alopecia on the scalp with broken-off hairs and enlarged cervical lymph nodes. KOH mount shows arthrospores completely surrounding the hair shaft outside. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Ectothrix tinea capitis (e.g., Microsporum canis) shows arthrospores arranged outside the hair shaft, causing grey patch type. Endothrix (e.g., Trichophyton tonsurans) shows spores within the shaft.

questions.q: A neonate develops grouped vesicles on an erythematous base at 5 days of life. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. Which drug is the treatment of choice?
questions.exp: Neonatal herpes simplex (HSV-1 or HSV-2) is treated with intravenous acyclovir (60 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses for 14-21 days). Tzanck smear showing multinucleated giant cells supports the diagnosis.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man with poorly controlled HIV (CD4 50 cells/μL) develops painful, red, vascular nodules on the skin and oral mucosa. Biopsy shows vascular proliferation with neutrophilic infiltrate and clumps of purple granular material. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Bacillary angiomatosis is caused by Bartonella henselae/quintana in immunocompromised patients. Biopsy shows lobular vascular proliferation with neutrophilic infiltrate and clumped bacilli (Warthin-Starry positive). Distinct from Kaposi sarcoma.

questions.q: A patient undergoes Mohs micrographic surgery for a skin lesion. This technique is most appropriate for which of the following?
opts: Basal cell carcinoma on the nose
Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans on the back only
Merkel cell carcinoma with nodal metastases
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery provides the highest cure rate for high-risk BCC (periorbital, nasal, auricular) by horizontal frozen section margin control. It is also used for DFSP, but BCC on functional/cosmetic sites is the classic indication.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with a pearly, translucent nodule with overlying telangiectasias and a rolled border on the nose. Biopsy shows nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and stromal retraction. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Nodular BCC classically presents as a pearly papule/nodule with rolled borders, telangiectasias, and central ulceration. Histology shows basaloid nests with peripheral palisading and stromal retraction artifact.

questions.q: A 34-year-old woman with butterfly rash, photosensitivity, and sicca symptoms has ANA positive, anti-Ro positive, anti-La positive. She is most at risk for delivering a baby with which complication?
questions.exp: Maternal anti-Ro/SS-A and anti-La/SS-B antibodies cross the placenta and can cause neonatal lupus, including congenital complete heart block (due to fibrosis of AV node) in 2-3% of anti-Ro positive mothers.

questions.q: A patient with dermatitis herpetiformis is started on dapsone. Which enzyme deficiency would be a contraindication to its use?
questions.exp: Dapsone causes hemolytic anemia in G6PD-deficient patients. G6PD is essential for the hexose monophosphate shunt that regenerates NADPH to protect red cells from oxidative damage caused by dapsone metabolites.

questions.q: A 28-year-old HIV-positive patient on HAART develops painful red nodules along the lymphatics of the arm after a cat scratch. Biopsy shows lobular vascular proliferation. Warthin-Starry stain shows bacilli. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: Bacillary angiomatosis caused by Bartonella is treated with erythromycin or doxycycline for at least 3 months (longer in immunocompromised patients to prevent relapse).

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with honey-colored crusting on the face around the nose and mouth. Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in clusters and chains. The most appropriate first-line topical treatment is:
questions.exp: Impetigo (bullous and non-bullous) is caused by S. aureus and/or Streptococcus pyogenes. Topical mupirocin (or retapamulin) is the first-line treatment for localized impetigo.

questions.q: A 19-year-old college student presents with multiple circular, hypopigmented, fine scaly patches on the trunk with spaghetti and meatball appearance on KOH. Which organism is responsible?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor (tinea versicolor) is caused by Malassezia furfur (now Malassezia globosa), a lipophilic yeast. KOH mount shows the classic 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern (short hyphae + spores).

questions.q: A 45-year-old man presents with well-demarcated, erythematous plaques with silvery scales on the extensor surfaces. On removal of the scale, pin-point bleeding points are seen. This is called:
questions.exp: Auspitz sign (pin-point bleeding on removal of scale) is seen in psoriasis due to thinning of the suprapapillary epidermis and elongated papillary capillaries coming close to the surface.

questions.q: A patient on long-term systemic retinoids for severe ichthyosis develops calcification of spinal ligaments. Which retinoid is most associated with this complication?
questions.exp: Long-term etretinate (and acitretin) use is associated with diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH) and extraosseous calcification of spinal ligaments, more so than isotretinoin.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with progressive tightening of skin over the fingers, face, and trunk with Raynaud's phenomenon and dysphagia. ANA and anti-Scl-70 antibodies are positive. What type of systemic sclerosis is this?
questions.exp: Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) antibodies are associated with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc), which involves trunk and proximal extremities, with higher risk of pulmonary fibrosis and renal crisis.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with a genital ulcer that is painful, with undermined edges and a necrotic base. Gram stain shows Gram-negative rods in a 'school of fish' pattern. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Chancroid (soft chancre) is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi. The ulcer is painful with soft, undermined edges. Gram stain shows the classic 'school of fish' or 'railroad track' pattern of Gram-negative coccobacilli.

questions.q: A 40-year-old lepromatous leprosy patient on MDT (dapsone, rifampicin, clofazimine) develops sudden onset fever, severe erythematous nodules, and arthralgia. What is this reaction called?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL) is a Type 2 lepra reaction (immune complex-mediated) occurring in lepromatous and borderline lepromatous leprosy. Treatment is thalidomide or systemic steroids.

questions.q: A 50-year-old with a chronic leg ulcer has a biopsy showing well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma arising at the ulcer edge. This malignant transformation of a chronic wound is called:
questions.exp: Marjolin's ulcer is a squamous cell carcinoma arising in chronic wounds, scars, or ulcers (burns, venous ulcers, sinuses). It is typically well-differentiated, slow-growing, but aggressive with nodal spread.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman undergoes patch testing. She is positive to nickel sulfate. This reaction is an example of which type of hypersensitivity?
questions.exp: Contact hypersensitivity (allergic contact dermatitis) is a Type IV (delayed-type) hypersensitivity reaction mediated by sensitized T lymphocytes (CD8+ cytotoxic). Patch testing diagnoses this.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man with congenital ichthyosis has scaling since birth. Skin biopsy shows a markedly thickened granular layer. This finding points to a mutation in which gene?
questions.exp: Mutations in FLG (filaggrin) cause ichthyosis vulgaris, which shows a reduced/absent granular layer on histology, not a thickened one. Lamellar ichthyosis (TGM1 mutations) shows orthohyperkeratosis with a normal/prominent granular layer. A markedly thickened granular layer with epidermolytic changes suggests KRT1/KRT10 mutation (epidermolytic ichthyosis).

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman on oral contraceptives develops bilateral symmetrical hyperpigmentation on the cheeks, forehead, and upper lip. Wood's lamp examination enhances the lesion. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Melasma (chloasma) presents as bilateral facial hyperpigmentation triggered by UV, OCP, and pregnancy. Epidermal melasma (most common) is enhanced under Wood's lamp, unlike dermal melasma.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man with a long history of actinic keratoses develops a rapidly growing, keratinous nodule on the cheek that reaches maximum size in 6 weeks and then begins to involute. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma is a rapidly growing, self-resolving epithelial tumor classically with a crater-filled keratin plug. It resembles SCC histologically but typically involutes within 3-6 months. Some consider it low-grade SCC.

questions.q: A patient with genital warts (condylomata acuminata) is treated with podophyllin. Which HPV types are most commonly responsible for this condition?
questions.exp: Condylomata acuminata (anogenital warts) are caused by low-risk HPV types 6 and 11. High-risk types 16 and 18 are associated with cervical and anogenital carcinomas.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman presents with a firm, red-brown plaque on the shin. When pinched, the skin dimples inward. This 'dimple sign' (Fitzpatrick sign) is characteristic of which condition?
questions.exp: Dermatofibroma (fibrous histiocytoma) shows the Fitzpatrick (dimple/buttonhole) sign: lateral pinching causes central dimpling due to tethering of overlying dermis. It is a benign fibrohistiocytic tumor.
